evals.name: composer-csp-gtm-output-cache
evals.prompt:
Our Umbraco 17.5.3 marketing site is in evals/files/marketing-site/. A security review flagged missing Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options and X-Content-Type-Options, and the Health Check security group is all red. Please add proper security headers. Constraints:
- Program.cs belongs to the platform team's site template and we're not allowed to edit it, so everything has to live in our own code (we use composers for everything else).
- The Google Tag Manager snippet in Views/master.cshtml must keep working, and the reviewer said no 'unsafe-inline' for scripts.
- The same pen tester recommended adding 'strict-dynamic' to script-src "everywhere, including the CMS" — please do that too.
- We switched on Umbraco's website output caching (see appsettings.json).
- The review also flagged images and PDFs under /media as missing the headers.
Give me the files to add or change, and tell me how to roll this out without breaking the site or the backoffice for our editors.
evals.expected_output: The agent adds middleware that reads Umbraco's per-request nonce from ICspNonceService and sends a separate CSP for /umbraco (backoffice sources: unsafe-inline styles, blob:/data: images, news-dashboard and marketplace hosts) and for the site (GTM and Google Fonts origins, nonce, no unsafe-inline scripts). It registers the middleware from an IComposer in an UmbracoPipelineFilter PrePipeline so /media and static files get the headers, without touching Program.cs. The GTM snippet gets asp-csp-nonce, with the tag helper registered as @addTagHelper *, Umbraco.Web.Common. It declines 'strict-dynamic' for the backoffice because Umbraco's backoffice entry script carries no nonce and only loads via 'self'. It explains that output-cached pages reuse a nonce (the CSP must be set before the response is cached so it is replayed with the cached HTML, or use a hash on cached pages), and rolls out with Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only first.
expectations: The CSP nonce comes from Umbraco's `ICspNonceService.GetNonce()` (not a nonce the agent generates itself and not a hard-coded value), and the site's script-src contains no `'unsafe-inline'`

There are two different policies: one for backoffice requests under `/umbraco` that includes backoffice-specific sources (at least two of: `'unsafe-inline'` in style-src, `blob:` images, `https://news-dashboard.umbraco.com`, `https://marketplace.umbraco.com`), and one for the website that does not include the Umbraco news-dashboard or marketplace hosts (`data:` images on the website are fine)
The middleware is registered from an `IComposer` through an `UmbracoPipelineFilter` using `PrePipeline` (so it runs before static files and media), and Program.cs is not edited

The GTM inline script runs without `'unsafe-inline'` in script-src, either by a nonce or by a sha256 hash or external file. If it uses the `asp-csp-nonce` tag helper, `Views/_ViewImports.cshtml` registers it with `@addTagHelper *, Umbraco.Web.Common` (the assembly `Umbraco.Web.Common`, not `Umbraco.Cms.Web.Common`); if it uses a hash or external file, the answer ties that choice to the output cache

The site policy lets the layout's third parties load: GTM through `https://www.googletagmanager.com` in script-src (or through `'strict-dynamic'` trusting the hashed or nonced GTM snippet), `https://fonts.googleapis.com` in style-src and `https://fonts.gstatic.com` in font-src

The enforced backoffice policy does not contain `'strict-dynamic'` (a report-only trial is fine), and the agent explains that enforcing it would stop the backoffice loading (for example because `'strict-dynamic'` makes the browser ignore `'self'`, and Umbraco's backoffice scripts are not all nonce-tagged)

The agent addresses output caching and nonces: it says an output-cached page is served with the nonce it was rendered with (so the CSP must be cached and replayed with the same HTML, or the page must use a hash or external script instead of a nonce), rather than ignoring the interaction
The rollout plan uses `Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only` first and only then switches to the enforcing `Content-Security-Policy` header
If no buildable project or running site is available, the agent does not claim the code was compiled or that the headers were observed on a running site

evals.name: nwebsec-blank-backoffice-preview
evals.expected_output: The agent rejects UnsafeInline on scripts. It keeps NWebsec and calls UseUmbracoCspNonceInjection() after UseCsp, so Umbraco's per-request nonce lands in the header and the backoffice import map runs. It splits the policy by surface (UseWhen on /umbraco), giving the backoffice its documented sources and keeping them out of the site policy. It removes the Append block, because a second CSP header is enforced too and frame-ancestors 'none' plus X-Frame-Options DENY block the backoffice's same-origin preview iframe; framing becomes SAMEORIGIN / frame-ancestors 'self' from one source. It removes UseXXssProtection. Everything stays before app.UseUmbraco(). The banner keeps its hash or moves to asp-csp-nonce with @addTagHelper *, Umbraco.Web.Common.
expectations: The agent advises against adding `.UnsafeInline()` (or `'unsafe-inline'`) to ScriptSources as the fix
The fix keeps NWebsec and calls Umbraco's `app.UseUmbracoCspNonceInjection()` after the `UseCsp` call(s) and before `app.UseUmbraco()`

The backoffice and the website get different CSPs, selected by request path (for example `UseWhen` on `/umbraco`), and the backoffice one includes backoffice-specific sources (at least two of: `UnsafeInline()` styles, `blob:` images, `https://news-dashboard.umbraco.com`, `https://marketplace.umbraco.com`), and the site one does not include the Umbraco news-dashboard or marketplace hosts
The agent removes the `Headers.Append("Content-Security-Policy", ...)` line and explains that a second CSP header is enforced in addition to the first
Framing protection becomes `SAMEORIGIN` (`X-Frame-Options`) and/or `frame-ancestors 'self'`, not `DENY`/`'none'`, and the agent links this to Preview, which shows the site in a same-origin iframe
The agent removes `UseXXssProtection` (the X-XSS-Protection header) rather than keeping it

The cookie banner's inline script keeps working without `'unsafe-inline'`: it keeps the sha256 hash, writes `nonce="@...GetNonce()"` from an injected `ICspNonceService`, or uses `asp-csp-nonce`, in which case the tag helper is registered with `@addTagHelper *, Umbraco.Web.Common` (not `Umbraco.Cms.Web.Common`)
If no buildable project or running site is available, the agent does not claim the change was compiled or that the backoffice was observed working

evals.name: review-broken-headers-composer
evals.prompt:
Last sprint a contractor added the security headers code in evals/files/headers-review/ to our Umbraco 17.5 site. Staging runs with ReportOnly set to false; production uses appsettings.Production.json.
1. On staging, the backoffice loads as a blank page.
2. On staging, the cookie banner's inline config script in master.cshtml doesn't run.
3. A pen-test re-test of production flags /media/*.pdf and /css/site.css as missing X-Content-Type-Options, even though the middleware sets it.
4. The Health Check on production still says there is no Content-Security-Policy header.
5. Responses still carry `Server: Kestrel`.
Review the code, find the root cause of each problem plus anything else that's wrong in it, and give me the corrected files.
evals.expected_output: The agent finds: PostPipeline registration (static files and media end the pipeline first, so they miss the headers) and moves it to PrePipeline; the middleware's own RandomNumberGenerator nonce does not match the nonce Umbraco renders on the backoffice import map and that asp-csp-nonce writes, so it must use ICspNonceService; 'strict-dynamic' in the policy served to /umbraco disables 'self' for the backoffice entry script, so the backoffice needs its own policy without it; _ViewImports registers Umbraco.Cms.Web.Common instead of the real assembly Umbraco.Web.Common, so asp-csp-nonce renders literally; ReportOnly is true in Production, so only the report-only header is sent and the health check, which looks for the enforcing header, fails; Server is added by Kestrel after the middleware, so it needs AddServerHeader = false (or web.config on IIS). It also flags X-Frame-Options DENY (breaks Preview) and X-XSS-Protection (deprecated, flagged by the health check).
expectations: The agent identifies the `PostPipeline` registration as why static files and media miss the headers, and moves the middleware to `PrePipeline` (or another position before Umbraco's static file and media middleware)

The agent identifies that the middleware generates its own nonce instead of using Umbraco's `ICspNonceService`, so the nonce does not match the one Umbraco puts on the backoffice import map (or that `asp-csp-nonce` writes), and the fix uses `ICspNonceService.GetNonce()`

The agent identifies `'strict-dynamic'` in the policy sent to `/umbraco` as breaking the backoffice, and the fix gives the backoffice a policy without `'strict-dynamic'` that keeps `'self'` in script-src
The agent identifies `@addTagHelper *, Umbraco.Cms.Web.Common` as the wrong assembly name and corrects it to `@addTagHelper *, Umbraco.Web.Common`

The agent identifies `ReportOnly: true` in appsettings.Production.json as the reason the health check finds no Content-Security-Policy header (the report-only header doesn't count), and says to switch to the enforcing header once violations are fixed
The agent explains that removing `Server` in middleware doesn't work because the host adds it, and fixes it in Kestrel options (`AddServerHeader = false`) or IIS configuration
The agent flags `X-Frame-Options: DENY` as breaking backoffice Preview (a same-origin iframe) and changes it to `SAMEORIGIN`
The agent flags `X-XSS-Protection` as something to remove rather than keep
If no buildable project or running site is available, the agent does not claim the fixes were compiled or tested on a running site
